project.objective: Did Juan Rodríguez Martínez and his wife Marcelina Garcia of Pozuelo, Albacete, Spain have a son also named Juan, who died in infancy in 1801, in addition to their eight known children (b. 1799-1822)?

questions.question: Did Juan Rodríguez Martínez and his wife Marcelina Garcia of Pozuelo, Albacete, Spain have a son named Juan who died in infancy circa 1801, in addition to the children already recorded in their family?
questions.rationale: This is the objective restated as a single-fact research question. Pozuelo (Albacete) Catholic parish registers survive for this period and include baptism and burial records that would document an infant death. The question is bounded in time (circa 1801), place (Pozuelo parish, Albacete), and fact-type (existence and death of a specific child). No evidence has yet been searched; this question opens the research.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: Searched the primary burial register for San Bartolomé, Pozuelo (Diocese of Albacete collection 1431011, image group 004090961_004) and found Juan Rodriguez buried 17 Feb 1801 with parents Juan Rodriguez and Marcelina Garcia named — directly answering the question. Both indexed baptism series for 1799–1821 were searched and returned no baptism for an infant Juan with these parents, consistent with the child dying before baptism or the baptism being in the unindexed volume (which was a fallback for a non-result, not needed). The Spain-wide baptism index (collection 1500692) also returned no baptism for the infant. A FAN siblings search across nine confirmed children's baptisms (1799–1822) mapped the full birth sequence and confirmed the infant Juan is an additional child outside that sequence. No civil registration existed in Spain until 1871; Catholic parish burial and baptism registers are the only relevant record types for this period. All relevant repositories and record types were searched. No conflicts identified. All 7 stop criteria met.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Met. The burial register (log_001/src_001) directly found infant Juan Rodriguez buried 17 Feb 1801 at San Bartolomé, Pozuelo, naming parents Juan Rodriguez and Marcelina Garcia. The FAN siblings search (log_007) confirmed the infant is additional to the nine-child sequence. A convincing, affirmative answer to the question was obtained.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: Met. The Diocese of Albacete collection (1431011) — the primary repository for Pozuelo parish records — was searched across the burial register (pli_001, completed) and two overlapping indexed baptism series (pli_002, completed). The Spain-wide baptism index (1500692, pli_005, completed) was also searched. Fallback items (pli_003 browse-only volume, pli_004 Spain Deaths index, pli_007 diocesan archive contact) were correctly skipped after the primary burial search succeeded. Civil registration did not exist in Spain until 1871; no other record type for this jurisdiction and period could document an 1801 infant death. Name variants (Rodriguez/Rodríguez, Garcia/García) were used in searches. FAN research on nine sibling baptisms (pli_006) confirmed the family sequence.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Met. The burial record is drawn from the Diocese of Albacete collection (1431011), an image-based collection of the original parish registers. The sibling baptisms (src_002–src_010) are likewise from original parish registers. No derivatives were substituted for available originals.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Met. Two independent units: (1) the burial register entry (src_001), created by the parish clerk at the time of burial with an unknown informant, directly names the infant and parents; (2) nine sibling baptism records (src_002–src_010), each independently created at distinct baptism events 1799–1822 with the parents as self-informants, collectively map the full birth sequence and confirm the infant Juan is an additional child. Informants for the burial record are distinct from the informants for the sibling baptisms.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: Met. The burial record (src_001, a_003) is an original record with primary information for the burial event — the parish officiant recorded it firsthand in an official capacity. The sibling baptism records (src_002–src_010) are also original records with primary information. At least one original record with primary information is present.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: Met. No conflicts were identified across any of the assertions. The burial date (17 Feb 1801) is consistent with the sibling sequence: Antonio Josef baptized 21 Dec 1800 and Francisco Josef baptized 4 Dec 1801. The birth-to-baptism interval is plausible for this parish and period. No discrepancies require resolution.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Low. Catholic parish burial and baptism registers are the only record types that document infant deaths in Pozuelo, Albacete in 1801 (civil registration began 1871). The burial register was searched and the child found. Both indexed baptism series for the relevant period were searched. No record type known to exist for this jurisdiction and period remains unsearched that could plausibly name a different result. The unindexed baptism volume (pli_003) was a fallback for a negative baptism result — irrelevant once the burial was confirmed. The diocesan archive (pli_007) was a last-resort fallback, also unnecessary given the positive result.

items.rationale: The parish burial register for San Bartolomé, Pozuelo, covering 1793–1826 is 95% name-indexed in the Diocese of Albacete collection (collection 1431011, image group 004090961_004, 255 images). Catholic practice required burial in the parish churchyard, so an infant dying in Pozuelo circa 1801 would appear here. Burial entries for minors name both parents, so the record would directly confirm or deny that Juan Rodríguez Martínez and Marcelina Garcia had a son named Juan who died in infancy. This is the highest-probability source for the question. Search under 'Juan' with parent names Rodriguez/Garcia, including spelling variants (Rodríguez, García).

items.rationale: FAN item: search the baptism records of the seven known children of Juan Rodríguez Martínez and Marcelina Garcia (b. 1799–1822) in collection 1431011. Reviewing the siblings' actual baptism entries will: (a) confirm the known children are correctly attributed to this couple in the Pozuelo parish register; (b) reveal the spacing of births, which may show a gap consistent with an additional child circa 1801; and (c) each sibling's baptism entry will name both parents by full name, confirming the couple's spelling and identity in the records as written. The infant Juan, if he existed, would appear in the birth sequence between siblings. This FAN search reveals evidence about the subject (the infant Juan) by establishing whether the family's birth sequence has a gap or anomaly around 1801.

If online sources (pli_001 through pli_006) neither confirm nor deny the infant's existence, contact the Archivo Histórico Diocesano de Albacete (Excmo. Sr. Obispo de Albacete, Calle Salamanca 10, 02001 Albacete; Tel: +34 967 214 478; obalbacete@planalfa.es) to request a search of any Pozuelo burial or baptism registers not yet digitized or not accessible online. The locality guide notes the Diocese of Albacete collection (1431011) is marked 'incomplete,' so some volumes may exist only in the physical archive. Write in Spanish, include the parents' names, the approximate date, and a request for photocopies. Fallback for pli_001 (primary burial register).

Spain Baptisms 1502-1940 (collection 1500692), surname Rodriguez, birthPlace Albacete, Spain, birthYearFrom 1799, birthYearTo 1803. 218 total matches, 20 examined. No baptism for an infant Juan Rodriguez son of Juan Rodriguez + Marcelina Garcia circa 1801 found in this page. Top hits include known sibling Juana Rodriguez Garcia (f., 06 May 1799, parents Juan Rodriguez + Marcelina Garcia confirmed) and multiple records of father Juan Rodriguez/Rodrigues appearing in siblings' baptisms (Victoriano, Severiano Roque, Francisco Donato, Cleofe, Maria Francisca — all bearing batch C89025-3). The infant Juan's own baptism was not recovered from this indexed collection; negative as to the primary question but positive for identifying sibling baptism batch C89025-3.

Batch C89025-3 in Spain Baptisms (1500692) — too broad. 754 Rodriguez records spanning the entire Pozuelo parish across all periods. Not useful for mapping the specific birth sequence of Juan Rodriguez Martinez + Marcelina Garcia. Superseded by the collection 1431011 targeted search below.

FAN siblings search: collection 1431011, surname Rodriguez, father Juan, mother Marcelina, b. 1795-1825. Top 9 results (score 6.03, batch C05354-8, all San Bartolomé, Pozuelo) confirm the full birth sequence: Juana (b. 06 May 1799), Antonio Josef (b. 20 Dec 1800), Francisco Josef (b. 04 Dec 1801), Maria (b. 02 Jul 1804), Bartholome Martin (b. 30 Jan 1809), Ana Juana (b. 12 Jul 1811), Vicenta (b. 26 Oct 1815), Severiano (b. 08 Nov 1817), Francisca (b. 09 Mar 1822). NONE is named Juan. The burial record for infant Juan (17 Feb 1801, log_001) places his death between Antonio Josef (Dec 1800) and Francisco Josef (Dec 1801), leaving no gap in the confirmed baptism sequence but confirming an additional unindexed son. Also found record ark:/61903/1:1:N3QG-Z53 ('Registro para Juan Rodriguez', father Juan Rodriguez, mother Marcelina Garcia, batch C05607-9, no date) — a candidate for the infant Juan's own baptism entry, to be read.

Candidate record for infant Juan's baptism — ruled out. The record (batch C05607-9) is a 1851 baptism entry for Juan Rodriguez (b. 10 Jun 1851, baptized 13 Jun 1851, San Bartolomé, Pozuelo). The searched persona (N3QG-Z53, p_11740743723) is the 1851 child's FATHER, whose parents are Juan Rodriguez + Marcelina Garcia — a later generation, not the circa-1801 infant. Not relevant to q_001.

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Proof Summary: Infant Juan Rodriguez, Son of Juan Rodríguez Martínez and Marcelina Garcia, Died 1801, Pozuelo, Albacete, Spain

### Research Question

Did Juan Rodríguez Martínez and his wife Marcelina Garcia of Pozuelo, Albacete, Spain have a son named Juan who died in infancy circa 1801, in addition to the children already recorded in their family?

### Conclusion

The evidence strongly suggests — at the probable tier — that Juan Rodríguez Martínez and Marcelina Garcia did have an infant son named Juan who was buried on 17 February 1801 at the parish of San Bartolomé, Pozuelo, Albacete, Spain. This child is an additional son beyond the nine children whose baptisms have been confirmed in the parish registers of the same parish between 1799 and 1822.

### Evidence

**The Burial Record (src_001)**

The primary evidence is a burial register entry from the Diocese of Albacete Catholic Church Records, 1504–1979 (collection 1431011, image group 004090961_004, 95% indexed), accessed via FamilySearch. The full citation reads:

> "España, Diócesis de Albacete, registros parroquiales, 1504-1979," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VTJ3-PBJ : accessed 10 September 2026), entry for Juan Rodriguez, burial 17 Feb 1801, San Bartolomé, Pozuelo, Albacete, Spain; image group 004090961_004 (parish burial register), Diocese of Albacete collection (1431011).

This record documents an infant named Juan Rodriguez buried at San Bartolomé, Pozuelo, Albacete, on 17 February 1801. The entry names his father as Juan Rodriguez and his mother as Marcelina Garcia — the same couple known from nine sibling baptism records spanning 1799 to 1822.

**Source classification:** The FamilySearch index/abstract is a *derivative* source (the indexed transcription, not a direct reading of the original register image, which is available at ark:/61903/3:1:S3HY-691S-222 but was not examined). The burial event itself — the date and place of burial — constitutes *primary information* recorded by the officiating priest or parish clerk in an official capacity (assertion a_003: `information_quality: primary`, `evidence_type: direct`). The parental names (assertions a_004–a_009) carry *indeterminate* quality because the informant who reported the child's name and parentage to the clerk is not identified in the indexed record; the original register image was not examined to confirm. This distinction matters for weighing: the fact of burial on 17 February 1801 at San Bartolomé rests on official first-hand recording; the identification of the parents rests on an unspecified informant, most likely a household member attending the burial.

**Identity of the parents.** The father named in the burial record, Juan Rodriguez, is identified as Juan Rodríguez Martínez (tree person 9634-PS9) on strong qualitative grounds: the same-person assessment against the tree mob (nine sibling baptisms 1799–1822, all at San Bartolomé, Pozuelo, Albacete) matches on primary paternal surname (Rodriguez), spouse (Marcelina Garcia), parish, and period. The compound tree surname Rodriguez Martínez — reflecting the standard Spanish two-surname convention, with Martínez being Juan's maternal surname from his mother Bicenta/Vicenta Martínez — accounts for the FamilySearch algorithmic score artifact (API returned −99, recorded as 0.0); this is not a qualitative conflict but a known limitation of the algorithm with compound surnames. The mother named, Marcelina Garcia, is identified as tree person 963H-MBM with a direct FamilySearch same-person score of 0.92 (pe_010), supported by name, spouse, parish, and period matching across all ten sources.

**The Sibling Baptism Evidence (src_002–src_010)**

Nine baptism records from the same collection and parish document the following confirmed children of Juan Rodriguez and Marcelina Garcia:

| Child | Baptism Date | Source ARK |
|---|---|---|
| Juana | 6 May 1799 | ark:/61903/1:1:N3M1-BS8 |
| Antonio Josef | 21 Dec 1800 | ark:/61903/1:1:N3M1-19Q |
| Francisco Josef | 4 Dec 1801 | ark:/61903/1:1:N3M1-1JT |
| Maria | 4 Jul 1804 | ark:/61903/1:1:N39M-M1F |
| Bartholome Martin | 31 Jan 1809 | ark:/61903/1:1:N39M-S4K |
| Ana Juana | 13 Jul 1811 | ark:/61903/1:1:N39M-3P8 |
| Vicenta | 26 Oct 1815 | ark:/61903/1:1:N39M-WCH |
| Severiano | 9 Nov 1817 | ark:/61903/1:1:N39M-4DV |
| Francisca | 10 Mar 1822 | ark:/61903/1:1:N39M-Z3P |

For the full citations to each record see research sources src_002 through src_010. None of these nine baptism records names a child Juan. The burial of infant Juan on 17 February 1801 — ten weeks after Antonio Josef's baptism on 21 December 1800, and ten months before Francisco Josef's baptism on 4 December 1801 — fits naturally in the chronological sequence and is consistent with a brief life ending before or shortly after baptism. No baptism record for this infant Juan was found in either indexed baptism series for the parish, which is consistent with the child having died before baptism (unbaptized children were sometimes buried with a brief record in the burial register rather than the baptism register) or with the baptism residing in the partially unindexed volume (image group 004090966_006, 0% indexed for 1792–1800) — a null search result there is inconclusive.

**Source classification (sibling baptisms):** All nine records are derivatives (FamilySearch indexed transcriptions of original parish registers; original images available but not examined directly). The baptism event information is *primary* (officiant recorded firsthand) and the parental name information is *primary* (parents appeared in person as self-informants, assigned `informant_proximity: self` or `household_member`). The evidence type for the sibling records, as it bears on the infant Juan question, is *indirect*: these records do not name Juan, but their collective completeness corroborates that the family's other children are documented and that Juan is not among them, reinforcing that the burial record describes an additional, otherwise unrecorded child.

### Correlation and Assessment

Two independent evidentiary units support the conclusion:

1. **The burial register** (src_001) directly and positively names the infant, his parents, the parish, and the burial date — this is the primary positive finding.
2. **The nine sibling baptism records** (src_002–src_010), each created independently at distinct events with the parents as self-informants, map the complete published birth sequence and confirm that no other child named Juan appears in the family's documented record. This corroborates the burial record's identification of the infant as an *additional* child.

The two units use different record types (burial vs. baptism), were created at different times by different officiants with different informants, and belong to the same collection series — they are not fully independent in origin (both are from San Bartolomé parish) but are substantively independent in creation circumstances and informant identity.

### Why Probable Rather Than Proved

The conclusion reaches *probable* rather than *proved* for two reasons:

First, the burial record was accessed as a derivative (the FamilySearch indexed abstract), not as a direct reading of the original register image (available at ark:/61903/3:1:S3HY-691S-222). The parental name assertions carry *indeterminate* information quality because the informant at burial is unidentified from the index. Examination of the original image could upgrade the informant analysis and potentially the information quality of the parental identifications.

Second, the sibling baptism records are also derivatives, and the one partially unindexed baptism volume (image group 004090966_006, 0% indexed) was not browsed image-by-image. It is possible — though not suggested by any positive evidence — that an additional baptism record for this infant exists there. The research-exhaustiveness agent determined this fallback unnecessary after the positive burial result, and the conclusion agrees; but the theoretical gap prevents the full GPS Component 1 exhaustiveness threshold for *proved*.

No conflicts exist. The chronology is internally consistent. The identification of both parents is strongly corroborated across ten records spanning more than two decades.

### Citation Limitation

All sources in this project were accessed as FamilySearch indexed abstracts (derivatives). The original parish register images are available on FamilySearch but were not examined directly. Future research confirming the parental names from the original register image (ark:/61903/3:1:S3HY-691S-222) would strengthen the informant analysis and could support a *proved* conclusion.

### Conclusion Statement

The evidence strongly suggests that Juan Rodríguez Martínez and Marcelina Garcia of Pozuelo, Albacete, Spain had a son named Juan who was buried at San Bartolomé, Pozuelo, on 17 February 1801, in infancy, in addition to the nine children whose baptisms are documented in the parish registers between 1799 and 1822. This conclusion is assessed at the *probable* tier.

# Locality Guide: Pozuelo, Albacete, Spain (1790–1830)

**Standard Place:** Pozuelo, Albacete, Castilla-La Mancha, Spain  
**Research period:** 1790–1830 (focus: circa 1801)  
**Parish:** San Bartolomé, Pozuelo

## Jurisdictional Context

Albacete province, in the Castilla-La Mancha autonomous community, was formally constituted in 1833 from the earlier Province of Chinchilla (created 1822). In 1801 the territory fell within the Kingdom of Castile under the Diocese of Albacete ecclesiastically. For genealogical research in the 1790–1830 period, the Catholic Church was the sole keeper of births, marriages, and deaths; **civil registration began nationally in Spain in 1871** (some municipalities from 1837), so no civil certificates exist for the target period.

## Primary Record Type: Catholic Parish Records

The Catholic Church was the primary record keeper until 1871. For Pozuelo, the relevant registers are held at the **Archivo Histórico Diocesano de Albacete** and are digitized in:

- **Spain, Diocese of Albacete, Catholic Church Records, 1504–1979** (collection [1431011](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1431011)) — index & images, 1,893,926 indexed records, 603,285 images.
